title: Per-tenant embedding dimension via an article_embeddings / memory_embeddings side table
background: The embedding vector dimension is pinned by the column type in exactly two migrations: priv/repo/migrations/20260410022854_enable_pgvector_and_add_embedding.exs:25 (ALTER TABLE articles ADD COLUMN embedding vector(1536)) and priv/repo/migrations/20260709000000_create_memory_stores.exs:101 (memories). Application.get_env(:loopctl, :embedding_dimensions, 1536) (config/config.exs:16) exists but is a CHANGESET VALIDATION ONLY (article.ex:490,506; memory.ex:281) - changing it does not change the column type, so 1536 is effectively hard system-wide. This is the blocker reported in #409: a local embedding model with a different native dimension (nomic-embed 768, bge 1024) cannot be used at all. The 2026-07-15 draft proposed a deployment-level single dimension; that is reversed here because the user who filed #409 is a HOSTED tenant, and a deployment-level dimension would force them off the hosted service to get a local model. CORRECTION to the 39 draft's premise: it is NOT true that 'HNSW inherits the column type so a mixed-dimension column is free'. pgvector refuses to build an hnsw/ivfflat index on a vector column with no dimension modifier, and a WHERE dim = N partial predicate does not supply a typmod - lib/loopctl/repo/hnsw_index.ex:125 emits USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops) which only works because the column today IS vector(1536). Two further grounded facts constrain this story: (a) CORRECTION to the round-1 text, which attributed the partial index to the wrong table: migration 20260709000300 is AddMemoriesLiveEmbeddingPartialHnswIndex - it is PARTIAL on WHERE superseded_by IS NULL over MEMORIES, not articles. superseded_by exists only on memories (memory.ex); ARTICLES have no superseded_by column at all - article supersession is modelled as status :superseded (article.ex:36 @status_values). So the live-row predicate that US-28.2 added must be preserved on memory_embeddings (mirroring memories.superseded_by), and the articles live predicate must be re-derived from articles.status. (b) semantic search, novelty and suggest-links run on HeavyReadRepo (BYPASSRLS) via the Loopctl.HeavyRead facade, whose guard!/2 (heavy_read.ex:642-660) RAISES unless every base-table source, recursively including joins and subqueries, carries a conjunctive tenant_id equality - RLS does nothing on that path.

story.as_a: a tenant whose privacy or cost constraints require a specific embedding model
story.i_want_to: choose an embedding model whose native dimension is not 1536 and have loopctl store and index those vectors correctly
story.so_that: I can run local or self-chosen embeddings on the SAME hosted instance, without forking to a self-hosted deployment

rationale: Moving the vector out of a fixed-width column onto a dimension-tagged side table is what makes per-tenant embedding models possible on a shared multi-tenant instance. It is the difference between 'loopctl supports local models if you self-host' and 'loopctl supports local models', which is the whole product question behind this epic.

acceptance_criteria.description: Vectors move to side tables article_embeddings(article_id, dim, embedding, live_denorm) and memory_embeddings(memory_id, dim, embedding, live_denorm), each tenant_id-scoped with RLS via the existing enable_rls/1 macro (repo/rls_helpers.ex:38-63, ENABLE not FORCE). Uniqueness is on (article_id, dim) / (memory_id, dim), NOT on the id alone: a dimension migration (US-41.2 AC-41.2.4) and the system corpus (AC-41.1.7) both require two dimensions to coexist for the same row, and recall is dimension-scoped anyway, so a bare unique(article_id) would force a destructive in-place overwrite and a total recall blackout across the re-embed window. Exactly one row per (id, dim) holds the current vector for that dimension; stale-dimension rows are dropped at cutover (AC-41.1.10). LIVE-ROW MARKER: the partial index predicate from US-28.2 (migration 20260709000300, AddMemoriesLiveEmbeddingPartialHnswIndex - MEMORIES, WHERE superseded_by IS NULL) is not expressible across tables, so a live_denorm marker is DENORMALIZED onto BOTH side tables: memory_embeddings.live_denorm mirrors memories.superseded_by IS NULL, and article_embeddings.live_denorm mirrors the articles live predicate derived from articles.status (articles have NO superseded_by column - supersession is status :superseded, article.ex:36). Sync is MANDATORY VIA A DATABASE TRIGGER (the repo's existing convention for this class of invariant - the audit chain uses PL/pgSQL triggers for exactly this reason); an application-level same-transaction write is permitted only as an additional convenience, never as the sole mechanism, because update_all, raw SQL, migration backfills and future graduation/merge paths bypass it and a desynchronized marker silently either lets superseded rows occupy ANN pool slots (the US-28.2 regression) or drops live rows from recall. Tests: (a) supersede a memory and an article THROUGH THE CONTEXT and assert each marker flips and the row leaves the ANN pool; (b) supersede via Repo.update_all (bypassing all application code) and assert the marker STILL flips.

Per-dimension ANN indexing is specified in a form pgvector actually accepts, VERIFIED against pgvector before the story is contracted: pgvector will not index an unconstrained vector column, so a WHERE dim = N partial index over a bare vector column is NOT an acceptable implementation. The implementation is ONE of (a) a typed column/table/partition per supported dimension (LIST partitioning on dim with a vector(N) column per partition), or (b) an expression index over an explicit cast - CREATE INDEX ... USING hnsw ((embedding::vector(768)) vector_cosine_ops) WHERE dim = 768 AND live_denorm - with the query using the IDENTICAL cast expression so the planner can match it. Whichever is chosen, each per-dimension index also carries the live-row predicate from AC-41.1.1, and the helper extending repo/hnsw_index.ex detects existence by EXACT INDEX NAME, not by access method (hnsw_index.ex:116-126's amname check would skip every index after the first, which is why 20260709000300 already had to detect by name).

Index DDL is OPERATOR/MIGRATION PLANE ONLY - never issued from the request path and never from set_llm_config. The instance publishes a FIXED set of supported dimensions on .well-known/loopctl (US-41.4 AC-41.4.10 - this story therefore DEPENDS on US-41.4, see dependencies); their indexes are pre-created by migration with @disable_ddl_transaction true + @disable_migration_lock true so CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY is legal, and the US-41.2 probe REJECTS any dimension outside that published set with the dimension-not-supported-by-this-instance remediation - that probe-side rejection is owned by US-41.2 AC-41.2.3 and is verified there (TC-41.2.5); THIS story verifies only the published set and the DDL-unreachability. A test asserts no API/MCP path issues index DDL.

A tenant's dimension is stored on the tenant (a tenant_embedding_dimension column added BY THIS STORY, so US-41.1's DATA MODEL is implementable without US-41.2's write surface - note this story does still depend on US-41.4 for the .well-known publication required by AC-41.1.3) and is readable via the API/MCP. Its v1 derivation is a STATIC model-to-dimension table shipped in this story, with :embedding_dimensions (1536) as the default for a tenant with no explicit model. US-41.2's config-time probe later reconciles with and OVERRIDES that table when a real endpoint reports a different dimension. Writing a vector whose length disagrees with the tenant's recorded dimension is rejected with a legible error naming both values - never silently stored or truncated.

Search and recall are dimension-scoped WITHOUT putting a join inside the index-ordered top-k. The ANN stage stays the documented filter-after-ANN shape (KB bd4a26b6, prod issue #172): a pure index-ordered inner top-pool over the embeddings relation whose WHERE clause contains ONLY predicates the partial index carries (tenant_id, dim, live marker), with every other filter and every join applied OUTSIDE that subquery. A cross-dimension similarity comparison must be impossible by construction (the inner pool is dimension-scoped), not merely unlikely.

The new relations satisfy the HeavyRead BYPASSRLS contract, not just RLS: every query that reaches article_embeddings / memory_embeddings through Loopctl.HeavyRead carries a CONJUNCTIVE tenant_id equality on the embeddings source itself (joined or subqueried), so HeavyRead.all/3's guard!/2 does not raise; memory_embeddings additionally satisfies guard_memory!/3's outermost subject_id equality. Tests cover BOTH paths: an RLS isolation test on Loopctl.Repo AND a test asserting guard!/2 accepts the real search query.

System-scoped articles (Article @scope_values [:tenant, :system], tenant_id nil, read by every tenant via 'a.tenant_id == ^tenant_id or a.scope == :system') have ONE DEFINED storage and recall story - the round-1 either/or is RESOLVED here, because leaving it open left a materially different product outcome undecided at spec time and one of the two branches was not implementable. TWO options are rejected explicitly. Rejected (a): article_embeddings.tenant_id nullable for :system rows. A NULL tenant_id can never satisfy the CONJUNCTIVE x.tenant_id == ^tenant_id predicate that AC-41.1.6 requires of every HeavyRead query - heavy_read.ex:13-23 documents and guard!/2 (642-660) enforces the rejection of both is_nil(tenant_id) and OR-broadened tenant predicates, and RLS does nothing on the BYPASSRLS path - so system rows would be unreachable on the semantic path, and the cheapest implementation-time 'fix' would be to weaken guard!/2, degrading tenant isolation on EVERY heavy read in the product. Weakening guard!/2 is forbidden by this AC. Rejected (b): embedding the shared canonical corpus at every supported dimension with an operator credential. No such credential exists: system articles have tenant_id nil, embeddings are per-tenant BYO and MANDATORY (embedding_client.ex:56-83 returns {:error, :no_api_key} with no fallback), and the global operator key was deliberately removed (comment at runtime.exs:385-390). Reversing that BYO-only decision is a separate, separately-argued story, not an implicit consequence of this one. CHOSEN: system-scoped rows are embedded ON DEMAND PER TENANT with the requesting TENANT's own embedding credential, written as ordinary article_embeddings rows carrying that tenant_id (article_id shared, tenant_id populated) - so the conjunctive predicate holds unchanged and no guard is relaxed. Until a tenant has materialized those rows, the system corpus is KEYWORD-ONLY for that tenant and the search response meta MUST say so explicitly (never a silent absence). A test asserts a 768-dim tenant recalls a system article semantically once materialized, and that before materialization the response meta reports the system corpus as keyword-only.

Cutover is explicit, not implied, and is SCOPED TO dim 1536. During the backfill window writes go to BOTH the legacy articles.embedding / memories.embedding column and the side table (dual-write); reads keep using the legacy column until a flag is flipped, and the flag may only be flipped after the backfill reports completion. DUAL-WRITE APPLIES ONLY TO dim = 1536, because the legacy columns are vector(1536) (20260410022854:25, 20260709000000:101) and pgvector HARD-ERRORS on inserting a 768- or 1024-length value - a dual-write mandate for non-default dimensions is physically unexecutable. Non-default dimensions are therefore side-table-only and are NOT available until the read flag flips for that tenant; the tenant-facing surface says so rather than failing opaquely. OPERATIONAL REQUIREMENTS, not left to the implementer: (i) the legacy-column write and the side-table write happen in ONE transaction, and a reconciliation pass detects and repairs side-table gaps (a crash between two separate writes leaves a legacy row the resumable backfill of AC-41.1.9 will skip, because the legacy row already exists); (ii) the read flag may only be flipped once EVERY node runs dual-write code - a Fly rolling deploy otherwise has old nodes writing the legacy column only while new nodes read the side table; (iii) the flip is REVERSIBLE, and reverting it is a supported operation for the duration of the dual-write window. A test asserts search results are unchanged MID-backfill (with only part of the corpus migrated), that a 1536-dim embedding written mid-backfill is present in both locations atomically, and that a simulated crash between the two writes is detected by the reconciliation pass.

Backfill migration moves every existing articles.embedding / memories.embedding into the side table with dim = 1536, is resumable and batched (the corpus is large - see epic 27 scale work), and leaves the old column in place but unused until a follow-up drop. Zero behavior change for existing tenants: same results, same ranking.

Changing a tenant's embedding model (and therefore dimension) is supported via an agent-triggerable re-embed backfill that reports progress through the existing job/anomaly surfaces, and it does NOT black out recall for the duration. It is documented as a one-time operation, NOT an online migration. Because AC-41.1.1's uniqueness is (id, dim), the OLD and NEW dimension vectors COEXIST during the window: recall keeps serving at the tenant's ACTIVE dimension - the QUERY embedding is generated against the endpoint/model that produced the active-dimension corpus, never against the pending one - and only flips to the new dimension when the backfill reports completion (US-41.2 AC-41.2.4), after which the stale-dimension rows are dropped. Without this, the moment the endpoint PATCH persisted, every query vector would be at the pending dimension while the corpus was still at the active one and NOTHING would match: a total search outage, i.e. exactly the corpus blackhole AC-41.2.4 exists to prevent. Rows not yet re-embedded at the pending dimension are excluded from PENDING-dimension recall rather than compared incorrectly, and any exclusion is reported in the search response meta so an agent sees WHY recall shrank.

The expected dimension is resolved ONCE per operation or batch and passed INTO the changeset as an option/attr; the validators at article.ex:490,506 and memory.ex:281 stay PURE (no Repo read, no process-dictionary lookup) so the ~100-article batch embedding path (US-37.4) does not become an N+1. A test asserts a batch of N articles performs no per-item settings query.

Query performance on the hosted default (dim 1536) does not regress. This is SPLIT into an automatable acceptance gate and a separately-tracked production observation, because a criterion requiring production DB access and a non-deterministic corpus can never be re-executed by the Epic 26 verification runner (US-26.4.2/26.4.3 - sandboxed, no prod access), so making it the acceptance gate would reduce the story's most important performance claim to a human self-assertion, which is exactly what the custody model exists to avoid. (i) ACCEPTANCE GATE (CI-checkable, part of the test suite): against a SEEDED corpus large enough to make the index the cheaper path, EXPLAIN the real semantic search query for each supported dimension and assert the plan shape - the per-dimension index is the chosen path, NO Seq Scan reaches the vector relation, and the assertion is made WITHOUT enable_seqscan=off (eligibility is not selection). Seed size and the seeding helper are committed with the test. (ii) PRODUCTION OBSERVATION (not an acceptance gate, tracked as an artifact report against this story): the implementing engineer runs AdminRepo.explain via fly rpc against the real corpus BEFORE merge and AFTER the backfill completes, attaches BOTH plan outputs verbatim to the story as an artifact report, and records p95 latency for the semantic search endpoint from the existing telemetry over the 24h before and the 24h after. 'Does not regress' means: same plan shape as (i), and post-cutover p95 within 20% of the pre-cutover baseline recorded in the same artifact. A regression beyond that threshold is an incident to roll back via AC-41.1.8(iii), not a finding to file.

test_cases.name: two tenants with different dimensions coexist and never cross-rank
steps: run semantic search as tenant B
expected_results: only tenant B's 768-dim vectors are considered
no error, no dimension-mismatch from pgvector
tenant A's rows are invisible (RLS) AND dimension-excluded

test_cases.name: per-dimension ANN index is CHOSEN by the planner on a seeded corpus (CI gate)
preconditions: a SEEDED corpus large enough that the index is the cheaper path
runs in CI - no production access, per AC-41.1.12(i)
steps: EXPLAIN the semantic search query for each dimension
expected_results: each plan uses the per-dimension index for its own dim
no Seq Scan reaches the vector relation
the assertion is made without enable_seqscan=off - eligibility is not selection
the production EXPLAIN of AC-41.1.12(ii) is an attached artifact report, NOT part of this gate

test_cases.name: backfill is resumable and lossless, and search is unchanged mid-flight
preconditions: articles and memories with existing 1536-dim embeddings (dual-write is dim-1536-only per AC-41.1.8)
steps: run the backfill
interrupt it midway
run a semantic search while partially migrated
write a new embedding while partially migrated
simulate a crash between the legacy write and the side-table write
re-run to completion
expected_results: mid-backfill search results identical to pre-backfill
the mid-flight 1536-dim embedding is present in BOTH the legacy column and the side table, written in one transaction
the simulated half-write is detected and repaired by the reconciliation pass - the resumable backfill alone does NOT catch it
every vector present exactly once at dim 1536 after completion
no duplicates from the re-run

test_cases.name: wrong-length vector is rejected legibly
steps: attempt to store a 1536-length vector
expected_results: rejected with an error naming expected 768 and got 1536
nothing written

test_cases.name: tenant isolation on BOTH the RLS path and the HeavyRead path
steps: query article_embeddings as tenant A via Loopctl.Repo
run the real semantic search query through Loopctl.HeavyRead
expected_results: tenant B rows are not visible (RLS policy enforced)
guard!/2 does not raise - the joined embeddings source carries a conjunctive tenant_id equality
an intentionally unscoped variant of the query DOES raise, proving the guard is load-bearing

test_cases.name: superseded rows leave the ANN pool - memories AND articles, including update_all bypass
preconditions: a full default-size pool of live MEMORIES plus superseded ones (the US-28.2 case, migration 20260709000300)
the same for ARTICLES, whose live predicate derives from articles.status, not a superseded_by column
steps: supersede a memory via the context (memories.superseded_by)
supersede an article via the context (status :superseded)
supersede a second memory via Repo.update_all, bypassing all application code
run recall for each
expected_results: each superseded row's live_denorm marker flips - including the update_all case, proving the DB trigger and not application code is the enforcing mechanism
no superseded row occupies a pool slot
the pool is filled with live rows - no silent under-fill

test_cases.name: system-scoped corpus is reachable at a non-default dimension
preconditions: a tenant configured at 768 dims with its own embedding key
steps: run semantic search as the 768-dim tenant BEFORE the system corpus is materialized for it
materialize the system corpus for that tenant (per-tenant rows, tenant_id populated, AC-41.1.7)
run semantic search again
assert the real query passes HeavyRead.guard!/2
expected_results: before materialization: the response meta explicitly reports the system corpus as keyword-only for this tenant - never a silent absence
after materialization: the system article is semantically recallable
guard!/2 does not raise and is NOT relaxed - the query carries a conjunctive tenant_id equality on the embeddings source, with no is_nil(tenant_id) and no OR-broadened tenant predicate

test_cases.name: index DDL is not reachable from the request path
preconditions: the fixed supported-dimension set published on .well-known/loopctl (US-41.4 AC-41.4.10)
steps: exercise every API and MCP write path this story introduces or touches
assert the published supported set matches the set of pre-created per-dimension indexes
expected_results: no CREATE INDEX / index DDL is issued by any API or MCP path at any role
the published set and the migrated indexes agree
the probe-side rejection of an unsupported dimension is owned and tested by US-41.2 (TC-41.2.5), not here - this story does not depend on the set_llm_config dimension surface existing

test_cases.name: batch embedding performs no per-item dimension lookup
preconditions: a batch of 100 articles to embed
steps: run the batch
count settings/tenant queries
expected_results: the tenant dimension is resolved once for the batch
no N+1

technical_notes: Verify the chosen per-dimension index form against pgvector FIRST (AC-41.1.2). If the expression-index-over-cast form does not plan as hoped, fall back to LIST partitioning on dim with a typed vector(N) column per partition - do not ship a design that assumes a bare vector column can be HNSW-indexed.
Keep :embedding_dimensions as the DEFAULT for a tenant with no explicit model, so existing config semantics survive.
pgvector cannot compare vectors of different dimensions - it errors. That is a safety net, not the design: the inner ANN pool must be dimension-scoped so the error is unreachable in normal operation.
Do NOT drop articles.embedding / memories.embedding in this story. Land the side table + dual-write + backfill first, verify in prod, drop in a follow-up so a rollback stays trivial.

Memories already use explicit (tenant_id, subject_id) predicates rather than relying on RLS alone (memory.ex:18-42) - preserve that pattern on memory_embeddings; HeavyRead.guard_memory!/3 requires it structurally.

Watch index build cost: HNSW builds are expensive at corpus scale. Per-dimension indexes are built CONCURRENTLY from a migration with @disable_ddl_transaction true and @disable_migration_lock true - never inline in a request.

Second brain: 'Decision: per-tenant embedding dimension (supersedes the 2026-07-15 deployment-level call)' records this call and the corrected cost analysis; KB bd4a26b6 records the JOIN-kills-HNSW incident (#172); KB 9c766ca7 records the three-repo split and the HeavyRead guard.
